Despite these favorable metrics, the stock currently sits at a mere 25% of its historical price range, implying potential for further appreciation [E4]. JINDRILL has demonstrated robust profit growth over various time horizons. Over the last five years, the company has achieved a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 102%, outperforming both the sector median of 51.3% and its own P/E ratio benchmark [E65]. This strong performance is further supported by the fact that JINDRILL's sales have grown at a YoY rate of 20% over the past year, as indicated in scanX signal engine data [E66]. However, it is worth noting that the company has experienced earnings growth deceleration over the trailing twelve months (TTM), with a CAGR of -62%, which could be seen as a negative factor [E70]. Despite this, JINDRILL's CWIP value has increased by 157.1% from the previous year, indicating significant capital expenditure and growth spend underway, suggesting future potential for earnings growth [E40].
